# Gasses Mundane gasses that easily found in nature. Some are used to breathe whereas others have minor uses.
## Air Mix
A mixture of gasses that is breathable to most species on the station. It consists of 21% oxygen and 79% nitrogen.
## Oxygen
A common gas, used by most species on the station to breathe.
Oxygen is an oxidizer, which means it supports combustion. This makes it both useful when fusing gasses in a burn chamber, and dangerous when mixed with flammable gasses. In spite of this obvious safety hazard, most species require it to live.
## Nitrogen
An inert gas, used in part with oxygen to create a breathable atmosphere.
Nitrogen is very stable and comprises most of a standard breathable atmosphere.
Some species like Slimes breathe nitrogen, with the Vox species requiring strictly nitrogen to breathe.
## Carbon Dioxide
A waste gas produced by most species on the station. A common byproduct of combustion.
Despite seeming useless, some departments use it in their line of work.
## Water Vapor
A common gas, produced by the burning of plasma and other processes.
Water vapor has a good specific heat capacity compared to other gasses, making it useful for moving heat around.
## Nitrous Oxide
An uncommon combination of oxygen and nitrogen. Primarily used as a anesthetic or recreationally.
Can be created by heating oxygen and ammonia, combining frezon and nitrogen, or exhalations from slime based organisms.
## Ammonia
A gas produced by the decomposition of bodies or exhalation from vox.
Can be condensed to create several useful chemicals, or heated with oxygen to create nitrous oxide and water vapor.
## Hydrogen
The most common atom in the universe.
Highly dangerous due to being flammable and invisible to the naked eye. Primarily produced by electrolyzing water as well as a byproduct of more advanced processes.
## Helium
The second most common atom in the universe. Has limited practical uses due being incredibly inert, but can be sold on the market for minor value due to the difficulty of isolating such an inert gas.
